features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows real production experience shipping AI-backed systems with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or degree attainment the letter presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing or owning agent-based systems, especially their architecture, guardrails, supervision, permissions, and control boundaries.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering problem-solving examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security work as helping internal developers and users through usable defaults, reduced friction, empathy, and collaboration.

levels.descriptor: Does not connect security work to helping other engineers.
Shows a general desire to reduce manual work, but not much empathy for developers using the tooling.
Explicitly discusses helping engineers or reducing toil through better security systems.
Strongly centers secure-by-default workflows, empathy for busy builders, or close attention to the needs of the teams being served.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how well the letter substantiates its claims with concrete examples, technical mechanisms, named artifacts, or measurable details rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's real production backend experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures whether the letter explains the concrete outcomes or effects of the applicant's work rather than only listing activities or responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Lists tasks with no visible outcomes.
Hints at benefit but remains mostly activity-based.
States clear outcomes such as reduced manual work, faster systems, or fewer bugs.
Shows strong leverage language, tying work to capacity, attention saved, or meaningful organizational effect.

features.name: Maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures emphasis on reliability, maintainability, testing, operability, and long-term care in security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a coherent, connected story or argument for candidacy rather than a disconnected checklist of claims.

levels.descriptor: Reads mainly as an inventory of credentials with little organizing idea.
Shows some motivation or theme, but the connection between past and role is loose.
Presents a clear professional theme, arc, or philosophy linking background to the role.
Delivers a memorable and tightly organized narrative that makes the fit feel intentional.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures whether the letter has a memorable, individualized voice rather than reading like a generic template.

levels.descriptor: The letter feels interchangeable, checklist-driven, or heavily templated.
The letter has some personal framing, but is still mostly standard and forgettable.
The letter has a noticeable voice or framing device that helps the applicant stand out.
The letter delivers a vivid, controlled narrative that is both memorable and well matched to the role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing hands-on adversarial practice, such as CTFs or similar exercises, that sharpens attacker-minded security judgment.

levels.descriptor: No adversarial practice outside normal work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional participation or casual practice without depth signals.
The letter shows regular or serious engagement in adversarial exercises.
The letter shows unusually strong external practice, such as near-top finishes or another high-commitment signal.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public codebases through upstream fixes, contributions, maintenance, releases, or care for software used beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance is mentioned.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or contributions.
Shows maintenance responsibility for a project or library used by others.
Shows active stewardship of an externally used project, including reviews, releases, roadmap, or a real user community.

features.name: Ownership seniority
features.description: Captures the degree of independent responsibility, initiative, and first-hand ownership the letter claims for the work it describes.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads mostly as passive, resume-like claims with little direct ownership.
The letter shows some first-person ownership, but mainly on isolated tasks or narrow pieces of work.
The letter uses clear builder language around multiple shipped systems, automations, or redesigns.
The letter repeatedly shows end-to-end ownership, architecture, delivery, and ongoing operational responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and relevance of self-directed projects or side work used as evidence beyond the day job.

levels.descriptor: No independent project work is mentioned.
The letter mentions a small utility, app, or lightweight side project.
The letter shows a substantial independent technical build beyond everyday work.
The letter shows an ambitious system built to tackle hard reliability, distribution, recovery, or failure-mode problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: The motivation could fit almost any software role and does not emphasize leverage.
The letter mentions scale or infrastructure briefly, but not as a core value.
The letter clearly values foundational tooling, secure defaults, or improvements inherited by many teams.
The letter builds a sustained case around organization-wide multiplier effects and the appeal of high-leverage platform work.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the depth, breadth, and concreteness of the applicant's professional experience shipping, maintaining, and operating production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how strongly and concretely the letter establishes Python as a serious production language for services, automation, tooling, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Role alignment
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter maps the applicant's background to this exact role's stated responsibilities, qualifications, or workflow needs.

levels.descriptor: The fit is vague and the reader must infer most of the relevance.
Some relevant matches are stated, but the mapping to the posting is incomplete or indirect.
Clearly connects several experiences to the role's stated needs.
Makes the match easy to verify, systematically covering most of the key qualifications or responsibilities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues through review, threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, remediation validation, or similar work.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation mission understanding
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter understands and is motivated by the role's mission of scaling security work through automation, workflow tooling, and organization-wide security infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: Frames the role generically as software or security work, with little sign of understanding the specific problem the team solves.
Mentions automation or security scale in broad terms, but without a crisp diagnosis of the underlying bottleneck.
Frames the work as reducing manual security workload or improving vulnerability handling at scale.
Articulates a precise thesis about the domain, such as scaling scarce expert judgment, treating vulnerability response as a systems problem, or multiplying one finding into fleet-wide protection.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the rigor and relevance of formal third-party security credentials or certifications cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Security engineering worldview
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful philosophy of security engineering as preventive, secure-by-default, resilient practice rather than mere interest or compliance.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface-level mechanical quality of the prose, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly belong to a broader recurring construct, such as coachability or general language breadth.

levels.descriptor: Shows no sign of wanting to grow through security collaboration.
Shows indirect openness to learning or collaboration.
Explicitly emphasizes learning from security engineers or deepening security craft on the job.
